title: Evaluating comorbidity scoring systems for flumatinib therapy in chronic myeloid leukemia: a machine learning and SHAP-based predictive analysis.
summary: Among 559 retrospectively studied patients with chronic-phase chronic myeloid leukemia treated with flumatinib, XGBoost predicted 12-month major molecular response (AUC 0.852). Adding CIRS-G comorbidity scoring produced the largest reported incremental AUC (0.078; p=0.006) among the evaluated scores. This single-center retrospective association may overestimate prospective validity.
ai_technology: XGBoost predicted 12-month major molecular response; SHAP interpreted nonlinear feature associations and interactions, while CCI, ACE-27 and CIRS-G scores were compared for incremental predictive value.
organization: Guizhou Medical University, China; Department of Hematology, People's Hospital of Qianxinan Buyi and Miao Autonomous Prefecture, China

evidence.tested: The publisher abstract reports retrospective data from 559 patients treated during 2018–2024, XGBoost AUC 0.852 for 12-month major molecular response, and the largest incremental value when CIRS-G was added to the baseline model (ΔAUC 0.078, p=0.006). SHAP analyses were exploratory; the study notes that temporal variation and retrospective design may overstate prospective validity.
evidence.unknown: The single-center retrospective model does not establish prospective performance or clinical benefit; the authors caution that temporal variation may overestimate validity.
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost predicted 12-month major molecular response; SHAP interpreted nonlinear feature associations and interactions, while CCI, ACE-27 and CIRS-G scores were compared for incremental predictive value.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
